subsystems.name: Rock feedstock
subsystems.role: supplies the silicate minerals that will react with carbon dioxide; reaction rate scales with surface area.

subsystems.name: Application to land
subsystems.role: spreads the powder thinly enough that it dissolves rather than crusts over.
parts: field mapping to match dose to soil and rainfall

subsystems.name: Soil reaction zone
subsystems.role: where the mineral actually weathers, driven by soil water and root-zone carbon dioxide.
parts: pore water carrying dissolved CO2 as carbonic acid

subsystems.name: Subsurface injection
subsystems.role: dissolves CO2 in water and pushes it into porous basalt so the reaction runs in about two years rather than millennia.

subsystems.name: Measurement and verification
subsystems.role: proves how much CO2 was actually removed, which is the hardest and most contested part.

buildSteps.title: Choose the mineral source
buildSteps.detail: Map basalt or olivine deposits near farmland and near low-carbon power, because grinding and hauling are the main emissions.

buildSteps.title: Crush and grind
buildSteps.detail: Rock is crushed then milled to a fine powder — often sand-sized or smaller — to expose fresh mineral surfaces.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the soil
buildSteps.detail: Measure soil pH, drainage, rainfall and existing carbonate so the dose can be matched to how fast the mineral will dissolve.

buildSteps.title: Spread the powder
buildSteps.detail: Standard agricultural spreaders apply a thin layer across fields, typically before a wet season when dissolution is fastest.

buildSteps.title: Let it weather
buildSteps.detail: Carbonic acid in soil water attacks the silicate grains, releasing calcium and magnesium ions and bicarbonate into drainage water.

buildSteps.title: Lock carbon into carbonate
buildSteps.detail: The bicarbonate either precipitates as solid carbonate in the soil or is carried to the sea, where it is stored for geological timescales.

buildSteps.title: Or inject into basalt
buildSteps.detail: For the subsurface route, captured CO2 is dissolved into water and pumped into fractured basalt, where it mineralises into carbonate within roughly two years.

buildSteps.title: Verify and account
buildSteps.detail: Drainage chemistry, cation budgets and tracers are used to estimate net removal, subtracting mining, grinding and transport emissions.

prerequisites.why: reaction rate depends on surface area, so milling is both the enabling step and the biggest energy cost.

prerequisites.tech: CO2 dissolution and injection into basalt
prerequisites.why: demonstrated in Iceland, where injected CO2 mineralised in about two years, and in a US basalt pilot, but not yet at large scale.
without trustworthy verification, neither carbon markets nor regulators can credit the removal.
the process only removes net carbon if grinding and hauling are largely decarbonised.
durability, additionality and trace-metal impacts need agreed standards before large-scale deployment.

pathway.milestone: field trials on farmland and a handful of basalt injection pilots
pathway.unlocks: real-world dissolution rates and first estimates of net removal.
credible carbon credits that pay farmers and project developers.

pathway.milestone: integration with existing quarries, mines and CO2-rich industrial streams
pathway.unlocks: cheaper feedstock and near-free CO2 for the injection route.

pathway.milestone: regional deployment across suitable farmland and basalt basins
pathway.unlocks: removal at hundreds of millions of tonnes per year, with soil benefits as a co-product.
